REVIEWLAB · QUALITATIVE ERROR ANALYSIS · 6 NOVEMBER 2026

Read beyond the score.

Three false positives, three false negatives, and a refined human review rubric.

False positives and false negatives here refer to the top-992 review queue on 9,916 held-out comments. The last included model score was 0.163. A human toxicity fraction ≥0.5 defines the reference-positive label. Model scores are not calibrated probabilities of policy violation.

These cases were deliberately selected to illustrate distinct failures, not estimate their prevalence. Explanations use actual model-feature contributions; causal interpretations and policy decisions remain qualitative judgments. The original model, labels, and benchmark metrics are unchanged.

CASE 1 · FALSE POSITIVE

Literal colours mistaken for a toxicity signal

Definitely - his outfit is sooo passé - it needs major updating. I like the idea of nice black trousers, white shirt and black jacket.

Model score: 0.422 · Toxicity annotator fraction: 0.0% · Rank: 427

Observed features: The words black and white contribute +1.05 and +0.48 to the linear score. Shirt pushes down, but does not offset those signals.

Interpretation: The model has learned broad lexical associations and does not reliably distinguish clothing colours from identity-related uses. This example does not reveal the author’s identity.

Proposed decision: No violation

Neutral description; no person or group is attacked.

Rubric change: Never flag a neutral colour or identity mention by itself. Identify the target and the actual abusive proposition.

Record ID: 84312aa2b32e74976cc9cba4208429c47d000bff48fe2913a0c8a123a9dab94c

CASE 2 · FALSE POSITIVE

Negation does not cancel the insult feature

Indeed, it's used, but paying a fair share doesn't mean someone is stupid. The TTC is $6 to use, why should the roads be cheaper?

Model score: 0.855 · Toxicity annotator fraction: 40.0% · Rank: 146

Observed features: Stupid contributes +1.51 to the word-branch score; overlapping character patterns also push upward.

Interpretation: A bag of short word and character patterns has limited ability to represent who is endorsing or rejecting an insult across a sentence.

Proposed decision: No violation

The sentence rejects the insult rather than applying it.

Rubric change: Read negation and speaker stance. Do not treat a rejected insult as an endorsed personal attack.

Record ID: d36de6a4ba0cf0dae52373cc78b0579b73e2dc4e6732374f0b31a2429b850f56

CASE 3 · FALSE POSITIVE

A quoted allegation is being challenged

"Aga Kahn a muslim imam connected to isis" Any proof of this ridiculous assertion?

Model score: 0.941 · Toxicity annotator fraction: 0.0% · Rank: 95

Observed features: Ridiculous, aga, proof, and muslim are positive word influences. A character fragment idi also pushes upward.

Interpretation: The scorer cannot reliably attribute the quoted claim to another speaker or recognise the author’s challenge. This is a plausible explanation supported by the feature contributions, not a proof of intent.

Proposed decision: No violation

In the visible text, the author asks for proof of the quoted allegation; the criticism targets the assertion.

Rubric change: Quotation is not endorsement. Assess the author’s stance; quotation marks alone do not exempt an endorsed attack.

Record ID: 888c2997508054b5849484653c67e42f3eba35780c59b8832f3c03b5aef8250c

CASE 4 · FALSE NEGATIVE

An indirect personal insult falls below the queue cutoff

Keith Olbermann: What an intellect deficient person you are. I wonder why any organization pays you to spout meaningless nonsense. You are one common sense deprived person.

Model score: 0.154 · Toxicity annotator fraction: 55.4% · Rank: 1,041

Observed features: The phrase intellect deficient is absent from the word vocabulary. Nonsense and you are push upward, while deprived and sense push down. The comment ranks 1,041, outside the 992 review slots.

Interpretation: The model represents the wording weakly; the fixed review budget then excludes a borderline score. A missed item is not the same as a zero-risk prediction.

Proposed decision: Violation

A person is directly demeaned for their perceived intelligence. Profanity is not required.

Rubric change: Include indirect and euphemistic personal attacks. Separate criticism of an argument from degradation of a person.

Record ID: b26417677a0048a7d3c0f9bcae2a9e0a9a79052c480005def8c6fa17985432da

CASE 5 · FALSE NEGATIVE

A contemptuous metaphor needs a target

Even the worms won't occupy his grave.

Model score: 0.019 · Toxicity annotator fraction: 50.0% · Rank: 5,828

Observed features: Worms is absent from the word vocabulary. His and grave are modest positive influences, while even the pushes down. The score is 0.019 and the rank is 5,828.

Interpretation: The metaphor’s degrading meaning is not captured well by the short lexical features. The reference annotation is exactly 0.5, so the benchmark class itself is a boundary case.

Proposed decision: Needs context / escalate

If directed at a real person, this is a degrading attack. The referent is absent, and mentioning a grave is not automatically a threat.

Rubric change: Consider figurative degradation. Require context for the target and distinguish an insult from a threat.

Record ID: e0b9e43bd4f402e09009d9b1b6fdf3d2f23d43cbc4c06862f0c23a022c37e55a

CASE 6 · FALSE NEGATIVE

Potential sarcasm about harm requires escalation

Yes, clearly these teenagers deserve death for simple trespassing and destruction of property charges.

Model score: 0.150 · Toxicity annotator fraction: 100.0% · Rank: 1,063

Observed features: Death and deserve push upward, but deserve death is absent from the word vocabulary. The score is 0.150 and the rank is 1,063.

Interpretation: This is a benchmark miss, but it does not establish that the correct policy decision is removal. The model also cannot supply the missing surrounding context.

Proposed decision: Needs context / escalate

The statement could endorse harm or sarcastically condemn an excessive response. The user selected escalation when intent is unclear.

Rubric change: For ambiguous sarcasm or quotation involving harm, escalate with a harm-context reason. Do not automatically infer endorsement or dismiss it as a joke.

Record ID: 1b1ebcae45b05094f7cfe6e38650339475213977c635ef0e4042fbb05672dddb

Review rubric v2

Decision order: target → stance → harmful act → missing context → action.

DecisionUse whenRecord
No violationNeutral identity/colour mentions; criticism of ideas; non-targeted profanity; clear rejection or reporting of abuse without endorsement.The visible context that makes the language non-abusive.
ViolationA clear endorsed personal attack, including indirect degradation; an identity-based attack; or clear encouragement of harm.The target, exact abusive proposition, and author’s stance.
Needs context / escalateAmbiguous sarcasm, quotation, referent, threat intent, or missing surrounding discussion. Harm-related ambiguity is escalated, as agreed with the product owner.What context is missing and why it would change the decision.
Urgent escalationA potentially credible, specific threat that needs qualified review. Do not infer credibility from a toxicity score alone.Relevant target, intent, specificity, and available context. This is a proposed workflow, not an implemented emergency system.
  • Profanity is neither necessary nor sufficient for a violation.
  • Quotation marks alone do not excuse an endorsed attack.
  • Do not assume a speaker’s identity from identity words in the comment.
  • Preserve original benchmark labels and record policy disagreements separately.
  • Model or rule changes must use development data, followed by new held-out evaluation. These six test cases are now diagnostic examples.
  • If urgent routing is added, include it within the declared review capacity and evaluate its trade-offs.

Annotation fields for the next review round

Comment ID; original toxicity fraction; target type; target excerpt; author stance; harmful act/category; proposed decision; evidence excerpt; missing context; reviewer confidence; reviewer ID; rubric version; adjudicated decision.

Double-label the initial 100-comment sample without showing model scores first. Resolve disagreements and report agreement before expanding. Keep a random audit sample separate from selected error examples.

Source: the frozen Civil Comments benchmark included in ReviewLab. Six-case record: dist/data/error-review.json. Original labels are not revised by this audit.
